body: The workaround is pretty bad, so this one is important.

Maybe @Sanne or @yrodiere have some insight about this? I think it has to do with Quarkus start up and the fact that a database might not be present. So, [Quarkus set a default dialect](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/33db72dbb0c56651a2a3da83c08af6e4b725a1b0/extensions/hibernate-reactive/deployment/src/main/java/io/quarkus/hibernate/reactive/deployment/HibernateReactiveProcessor.java#L247).
Maybe I can just update the default for Sql Server?
Ah, I think this class is just behid compared to the ORM one. I will try to update it

Quarkus sets the dialect and DB version at build time. Technically during static init, but the rule in Quarkus is that anything done at static init must be assumed to happen at build time -- I tried to challenge that, but no luck so far as it implies degraded functionality in native mode compared to JVM mode.

Anyway, the thing is: Hibernate ORM in Quarkus cannot detect the version running on the database server, since the version is set in stone before the application starts.

By default it will assume the minimal supported version, i.e. SQL Server 2016: 

https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/0a6d90945ef528d30dbe0800f28b08c81f87d347/extensions/hibernate-orm/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/hibernate/orm/runtime/config/DialectVersions.java#L20

Setting a custom dialect is not the correct solution. If you want a more recent version, you can configure it explicitly:

https://quarkus.io/guides/hibernate-orm#hibernate-dialect

Now I'm having a look why the default dialect version is wrong in your reproducer... I suspect it might be related to a different handling of `jakarta.persistence.database-product-version` in Hibernate Reactive compared to Hibernate ORM? Checking.

@DavideD It looks like the problem is in the Hibernate Reactive extension in Quarkus; namely `HibernateReactiveProcessor` doesn't have an equivalent to `io.quarkus.hibernate.orm.deployment.HibernateOrmProcessor#collectDialectConfig` in the Hibernate ORM extension.

> Setting a custom dialect is not the correct solution. If you want a more recent version, you can configure it explicitly:
